i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Governing problem: how Union financial support from the Fund is allocated to Member States on the basis of approved Social Climate Plans, released against performance and protected against misuse. Scale: Union level (Commission) and Member State level (with national control bodies). Domain: financing of the social impacts of including buildings and road transport in the emissions trading system. Jurisdiction: European Union. Interval: 2026-2032 with payments until 31 December 2033.
i2_coupling_description: Qualified procedural dependency among the S by explicit cross-reference: (a) SC-01 to SC-03: A19.P1 (agreement after the positive decision of Article 17), A20.P1 and A20.P2 (milestones and targets as set in the Article 17 decision), A17.P2(b) (instalments in accordance with Article 20); (b) SC-03 to SC-04: A21.P2 (the Article 19 agreements provide for the control obligations), A21.P2(c) (accompaniment of payment requests), A21.P4 (reduction and recovery right in the agreements), A17.P3(c) (additional internal-control measures before the first payment), A21.P1 and Annex III; (c) SC-01 to SC-07: A16.P2 (assessment of transfers requested under Article 11), A11.P2; (d) SC-02 nested in SC-01 via A5.P3.
i3_configurational_consequence: Conditional sequence attributable to the whole: disbursement of Fund resources is legally tied, within W, to a prior Commission decision on the Plan, an agreement and a milestone-based assessment, with national and Union control relations attached to the payment request; the Commission is the single named decision-taker at the decision points (Plan decision; individual payment decision) while Member States, national authorities and Union control bodies hold submission, control and access roles.
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer: ARCHITECTURE ARCH-01 (emergent/whole property: conditional sequence of authorisation and control across SC-01, SC-03, SC-04). Inferential rule: the sequence is read from the cross-referenced conditions identified in I2 (not from reachability, from a common actor or from graph connectivity) and is recorded as a configuration of stated conditions, not as a path property or a score.
i4_evidence_searched: CL cov (all units read); CL cent_sc1, cent_sc3, thresholds, review, private, implact and necessary (absence claims); CL extcov (outside sources not searched).
i4_rival_grouping: Rival groupings: (i) SC-01 and SC-03 as two separate architectures joined only at the Article 17 decision; (ii) SC-04 as a separate national internal-control architecture; (iii) merger with ARCH-02 and ARCH-03 into one whole-instrument architecture (not warranted: see those candidates).
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If rules outside W provided other payment routes or different conditions, the sequence of A19-A20 could be bypassed; the claim is therefore stated within the declared corpus W only. The coupling of SC-07 would weaken if the rules of the receiving funds (Regulation (EU) 2021/1060) separated transferred resources from Article 17 decisions.
outcome_basis: I1 to I4 each stated and evidenced within W: the governing problem and scale are fixed by A1, A3, A7, A10 and A20.P8; the coupling is a qualified procedural dependency resting on explicit cross-references independent of any expected global property; the configurational consequence is a conditional sequence of decision points; boundaries, rival groupings and unresolved external dependencies are stated. The outcome is scoped to the declared corpus and queued for human review because the I2/I3 thresholds are unvalidated.

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Governing problem: monitoring and evaluation of implementation and results of the Fund (Member State reporting, Commission monitoring and evaluation, reports to Union institutions). Scale: Member State and Union levels. Jurisdiction: European Union. Interval: from the start of implementation of the Plans to the ex post evaluation by 31 December 2033.
i2_coupling_description: Qualified procedural dependency internal to SC-05: A27.P1 evaluates 'taking into account the results of the first reports submitted by Member States in accordance with Article 24'; A24.P4 requires the Commission to use the Annex IV indicators that A24.P1 requires Member States to include. Interface with ARCH-01: A6.P1(m) and A17.P2(d)-(e) require the Plan and the decision to contain monitoring arrangements and the Annex IV indicators.
i3_configurational_consequence: Feedback of implementation information into review of the instrument: the evaluation report is legally conditioned on Member State reports and assesses the continued relevance of objectives, measures and assigned revenues (A27.P2(d)), with a duty to propose amendments where appropriate (A27.P1).
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer: ARCHITECTURE ARCH-02 (emergent/whole property: reporting-to-evaluation feedback). Inferential rule: conditional sequence read from the explicit cross-reference A27.P1 to Article 24; no exercise and no transmission is inferred from reachability.
i4_evidence_searched: CL cov; CL monitor link; CL eval_assess; CL extcov.
i4_rival_grouping: Rival grouping: monitoring as a stage inside ARCH-01 (the payment assessment of A20 verifies milestones and targets); not supported by a legal link between A24 reports and A20 (CL monitor link), but the Annex IV interface of the Plan content and decision ties the two sets of provisions.
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If A24 reports were legally linked to payment assessment, SC-05 would fall inside ARCH-01; if the Annex IV interface were disregarded, SC-05 would be a distinguishable candidate. The coupling with ARCH-01 rests on a mandatory interface through the Plan content and decision, not on a shared actor alone.
outcome_basis: I1 to I4 are satisfied within SC-05; the candidate overlaps ARCH-01 through the source-supported mandatory interface (Annex IV indicators referred to in A6.P1(m), A17.P2(d)-(e), A24.P1 and A24.P4). The intersection is not treated as a separate architecture. Queued for human review because the I2/I3 thresholds are unvalidated.

i1_governing_problem_and_scale: Governing problem: parliamentary information and dialogue with the Commission on the Fund, stated in A26.P1 as enhancing dialogue between Union institutions and ensuring greater transparency and accountability. Scale: Union institutional level. Jurisdiction: European Union.
i2_coupling_description: Coordination or communication internal to SC-06: A26.P2 refers to 'the views expressed through the social climate dialogue' (A26.P1).
i3_configurational_consequence: Candidate property: an accountability interface of the Commission toward the competent European Parliament committees. Forum, channel, questioning capacity and a duty to take account are evidenced; the duty to explain, assessment capacity and consequences are not stated; the property can be attributed only as answerability with indeterminate sufficiency.
i3_bearer_and_rule: Bearer: ARCHITECTURE ARCH-03 (accountability structure). Inferential rule: DR-17 elements assembled in qr_acc_ep; no element is inferred from exercise or from the stated purpose.
i4_evidence_searched: CL cov; CL discharge; CL eval_assess; CL extcov.
i4_rival_grouping: Rival grouping: the dialogue together with A25.P1 and A25.P3 as one parliamentary-information architecture, or together with the discharge procedure of Article 319 TFEU (outside W).
i4_boundary_sensitivity: If the discharge procedure outside W were included, accountability toward the Parliament could be fuller; within W the claim cannot be completed.
outcome_basis: I3 is indeterminate (accountability elements missing) and the constitutive external dependency on the discharge procedure touches the claim; no architecture is asserted for this candidate (stopping rule). The question is queued as HQ-ACCOUNT.
